blocks.text: The chapter deliberately joins the feeding, manna, coming to Jesus, believing, eating his flesh and drinking his blood, abiding, death, and life. Readers have understood this network in different ways: as a claim about Jesus’ identity, as wisdom-like teaching, as sacramental language, or through combinations of these approaches. The chapter itself keeps returning to belief and life while also intensifying its bread imagery, so the disputed language should be read as part of the whole movement rather than isolated from it. John’s “I am the bread of life” saying also works within a larger pattern in which such sayings can carry ordinary identification, symbolic meaning, scriptural echoes, and claims about divine agency; this particular context must guide its interpretation.

sections.title: Reading the Bread of Life Discourse
